To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
129;B 6 Pomc null mice produce abundant e umelanin hair pigment in skin despite their congenital lack of melanocortins.

the absence of proopiomellanocortin (the gene encoding the precursor to melanocyte-stimulating hormone and other peptides that control pigmentation) in mice does not result in the expected coat color change.

129;B 6 Pomc-/- mutant mice produce abundant black hair pigmentation, despite their congenital deficiency in melanocortin peptides, and that the mechanism of this eumelanin production is not yet known.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the melanocortins, in particular alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone, in hair pigmentation.
the role of the proopiomelanotropin (POM) gene in the regulation of melanin synthesis in the hair follicle.
the development of novel strategies for treating obesity and other disorders of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
melanocortin peptides are not required for the initiation and maintenance of eumelanogenesis.
the melanocortins are not required for hair pigmentation.
melanin pigmentation is not dependent on POMC-derived melanocortin peptides in mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the melanocortins are not essential for eumelanogenesis, and that their role in hair pigmentation is to regulate the ratio of eumelanins to pheomelanins.
the mouse melanocortex, which is the neural crest-derived neural crest-melanoblast-melanocyte-melanin axis, is a complex system that is not completely understood.
melanocortin receptors are not essential for hair pigmentation, and that the melanocyte-stimulating hormone is not the only factor controlling melanogenesis in the hair follicle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mouse melanocorticoid receptor 1 has intrinsic activity, which is not surprising given its high degree of sequence similarity to other melanocorticoid receptors.
the mouse melanocorin receptor has enough basal activity to trigger melanogenesis in hair follicles in the absence of alpha-MSH.
the absence of POC peptides is compatible with normal pigmentation, which suggests that the role of POC-derived peptides in the control of pigmentation is not as critical as previously thought.
